Thinking through this as myself...

I have been farming this land for over 40 years. My father farmed it before me, and his father before that. In Quzhou, everybody around me grows winter wheat and summer maize on the same fields — rotate them, one after the other, year after year. I am not going to change that. That is what the soil here suits, that is what I know how to do, and that is what the grain buyers expect.

My land is about 10 mu. After my youngest son moved to Baoding for work, I am managing it mostly alone, so I cannot afford to experiment or take risks. I am 60. My back is not what it was.

For wheat, I will plough deep this autumn before sowing — I still believe in turning the soil properly, not this lazy rotary business my neighbor does. I will use the Jimai variety that the township agricultural station has been selling for years. Good, reliable seed. I will water it three times: once in late winter before the freeze locks in hard, once at jointing, once at grain filling. I always apply urea in two splits — base dressing at planting and top dressing at jointing. Phosphorus and potash go in all at once as base.

For maize, right after I harvest the wheat in June, I rotary till the stubble down and sow hybrid seed — I have been using Zhengdan 958 for many years, it is dependable. Summer rains usually handle irrigation, but I keep one irrigation ready if July turns dry. Maize does not need much spraying — just one herbicide pass early on.

I keep one mu of vegetables near the house — garlic, cabbage, some beans — for the family and to sell a little at the village market.
